gen-gf-bellota-gf-alegreya: Alegreya reads like a well-thumbed novel, its curves flexing gently and its apertures staying stubbornly open. Bellota's rope-like, single-width line and far-reaching s add a bolder, more singular streak to that bookish warmth.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-alegreya-sc: Bellota brings a display heading drawn with one unvarying line, its s ends hanging far from the spine. Alegreya SC, a serif, softens that with a tilted-nib gradient, and the two sit together like a decree beside a footnote.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-alike-angular: Alike Angular is a serif with a subtle thick and thin cadence. Its letters stay held open rather than curled shut, so a long passage moves along steadily, never reaching for razor-fine hairlines, while Bellota's heading keeps its line thickness constant.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-alyamama: Bellota draws everything as a rope-thin outline, with no thick or thin parts anywhere. Alyamama, a serif, adds a quiet variation in line weight within each letter, and its curve endings stay well apart, which gives the pairing a refined, traditional steadiness.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-ancizar-serif: Distinctive and commanding, Bellota sets its hanging-s headings at a single stylus width. Ancizar Serif follows with a bookish serif that has a faint pull between heavy verticals and lighter horizontals, and its gaping c stays visible at any size.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-andada-pro: Andada Pro is a classic serif with medium-range stroke modulation and counters that let the eye slip in and out easily. It makes a bookish partner for Bellota, whose headings have no pinched joins at all.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-aref-ruqaa: Aref Ruqaa is a dignified serif with open bowls that welcome the eye and a mild stress in its o and e. Bellota's flat, unmodulated stroke makes a bolder neighbor.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-aref-ruqaa-ink: Soft-edged, bookish and open. Bellota's heading is the stronger of the two at making a statement with its unmodulated line, while Aref Ruqaa Ink, a classic serif, does its best work with a mild shift from heavy stems to lighter curves.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-average: Average has gaping e mouths and reed-pen thickening. Bellota excels at bold, bent-rope headlines of unvarying line, while Average, a classic serif, does its best work in text where stroke weight shifts noticeably but never dramatically.
gen-gf-bellota-gf-besley: Besley is a dignified text serif with sturdy hairlines. Bellota's headings have no vertical emphasis and no horizontal thinning, so they sit above Besley's moderate stems and slightly thinner crossbars as a rounder, more uniform counterpart.
